prompts.L1:
Please polish the following text to make it more eloquent and professional, keeping all original information unchanged:

An exhaust treatment system and method for the treatment of an exhaust stream from a combustion engine are provided. A first oxidation of compounds comprising one or more of nitrogen, carbon and hydrogen in the exhaust stream is carried out by a first oxidation catalyst. Further, a value (NO2_1/NOx_1)det for a ratio between a first amount of nitrogen dioxide and a first amount of nitrogen oxides leaving said first oxidation catalyst is determined. Active control of at least one parameter related to the combustion engine is carried out, based on the determined value, so that the ratio is impacted. A first additive is supplied into the exhaust stream, following which a first reduction of the first amount of nitrogen oxides is carried out through a catalytic reaction in a catalytic filter, which consists of a particulate filter with an at least partly catalytic coating with reduction characteristics. The catalytic filter is arranged for catching and oxidizing of soot particles, and to carry out the first reduction of the first amount of nitrogen oxides using the first additive.

An exhaust treatment system is configured to treat an exhaust stream generated by a combustion engine. The exhaust stream first passes through a first oxidation catalyst, where selected exhaust components are oxidized and the chemical composition of the exhaust gas is modified.

The system determines a ratio between nitrogen dioxide and total nitrogen oxides leaving the first oxidation catalyst. This ratio provides information about the state of the exhaust gas and the effectiveness of the oxidation process occurring in the catalyst.

Based on the determined ratio, the system actively controls at least one operating parameter of the combustion engine. By adjusting the engine parameter, the system can influence the composition of the exhaust stream, including the relative amounts of nitrogen dioxide and other nitrogen oxides. This allows the exhaust treatment process to be optimized under different engine operating conditions.

A first additive is also supplied into the exhaust stream. The additive is introduced to support the reduction of nitrogen oxides downstream in the exhaust treatment system.

The exhaust stream then passes through a catalytic particulate filter. The filter captures soot particles contained in the exhaust gas and promotes oxidation of those particles. At the same time, the catalytic particulate filter uses the supplied additive to reduce nitrogen oxides in the exhaust stream. In this way, the system combines particulate removal, soot oxidation, and nitrogen oxide reduction in an integrated exhaust treatment process.
outputs.L4:
An exhaust treatment system for a combustion engine is designed to reduce multiple pollutants present in the exhaust gas stream, including nitrogen oxides and particulate matter such as soot. The system includes a first oxidation catalyst positioned in the exhaust line downstream of the engine. As exhaust gas passes through this catalyst, certain components of the exhaust are oxidized, and the relative amount of nitrogen dioxide in the total nitrogen oxides content can be influenced. In particular, the system is concerned with the ratio of NO₂ to total NOx, where NOx includes nitric oxide and nitrogen dioxide.

To monitor and regulate this condition, the exhaust system includes a device or method for determining the NO₂/NOx ratio in the exhaust stream. This information is supplied to a control unit, which can adjust one or more operating parameters of the combustion engine. Such parameters may include fuel injection timing, fuel quantity, air-to-fuel ratio, exhaust gas recirculation rate, boost pressure, or other settings that affect exhaust composition and temperature. By actively controlling these engine parameters, the system can bring the NO₂/NOx ratio into a desired range that supports effective downstream exhaust treatment.

The system may also include an additive injection device arranged to introduce a reducing agent or other additive into the exhaust gas. This additive can assist in the catalytic reduction of nitrogen oxides in a downstream treatment component. For example, the additive may be ammonia, a urea solution that decomposes to form ammonia, a hydrocarbon, or another suitable reagent depending on the type of catalyst used. The quantity of additive injected can be controlled in response to the measured or estimated NO₂/NOx ratio, engine operating conditions, exhaust temperature, and NOx concentration.

Downstream of the oxidation catalyst and additive injection location, the exhaust gas passes through a catalytic particulate filter. This filter traps soot and other particulate matter while also providing catalytic activity for further exhaust purification. The trapped soot can be oxidized, particularly when sufficient NO₂ is present, allowing the filter to regenerate and maintain its filtering capacity. At the same time, the catalytic coating or material associated with the filter can promote the reduction of nitrogen oxides, especially when the exhaust composition and additive dosing are properly controlled.

By coordinating oxidation, NO₂/NOx ratio monitoring, engine-parameter adjustment, additive injection, and particulate filtration, the system provides an integrated approach to exhaust aftertreatment. Controlling the NO₂/NOx ratio helps create favorable conditions for both soot oxidation and NOx reduction. The particulate filter removes solid particles from the exhaust, while the catalyst functions reduce harmful nitrogen oxides before the exhaust is released into the atmosphere. As a result, the system improves overall exhaust purification and can help combustion engines meet stricter emissions requirements while maintaining reliable operation.

counterfactuals.prompt: Generate a technical patent claim/abstract describing a method for treating diesel engine exhaust where NO, NO2, hydrocarbons, and carbon compounds are oxidized, the NO2/NOx ratio after the DOC is controlled, and urea or another additive is used in a catalytically coated particulate filter.
counterfactuals.output:
## Abstract

A method for treating exhaust gas from a diesel engine comprises directing an exhaust gas stream containing nitrogen monoxide (NO), nitrogen dioxide (NO₂), hydrocarbons, carbon monoxide, and particulate carbon compounds through a diesel oxidation catalyst (DOC) configured to oxidize at least a portion of the NO to NO₂ and to oxidize hydrocarbons and carbon monoxide. The oxidation activity of the DOC is selected or regulated such that a predetermined NO₂/NOx ratio is established downstream of the DOC. The exhaust gas is then contacted with an additive comprising urea, ammonia, an ammonia precursor, or another nitrogen-containing reducing agent, and passed through a particulate filter having a catalytic coating. In the catalytically coated particulate filter, soot and other carbonaceous particulates are retained and oxidized, while nitrogen oxides are converted at least in part by selective catalytic reduction and/or other catalytic reactions promoted by the coating and the additive. The controlled NO₂/NOx ratio enhances particulate oxidation and NOx conversion efficiency while limiting excessive NO₂ emissions.

## Exemplary Patent Claim

1. **A method for treating exhaust gas of a diesel internal combustion engine**, the method comprising:  

   passing an exhaust gas stream comprising nitrogen monoxide (NO), nitrogen dioxide (NO₂), nitrogen oxides (NOx), hydrocarbons, carbon monoxide, and carbon-containing particulate matter through a diesel oxidation catalyst;  

   oxidizing, in the diesel oxidation catalyst, at least a portion of the hydrocarbons and carbon monoxide and oxidizing at least a portion of the nitrogen monoxide to nitrogen dioxide;  

   controlling an oxidation activity of the diesel oxidation catalyst such that an NO₂/NOx ratio in the exhaust gas downstream of the diesel oxidation catalyst is maintained within a predetermined range;  

   introducing into the exhaust gas, downstream of the diesel oxidation catalyst, an additive selected from urea, ammonia, an ammonia precursor, a hydrocarbon reducing agent, or a mixture thereof; and  

   passing the exhaust gas and the additive through a particulate filter comprising a catalytic coating,  

   wherein the particulate filter traps carbon-containing particulate matter, the catalytic coating promotes oxidation of at least a portion of the trapped carbon-containing particulate matter, and the additive participates in catalytic conversion of at least a portion of the nitrogen oxides in the exhaust gas.

2. **The method of claim 1**, wherein the predetermined NO₂/NOx ratio is selected to promote passive regeneration of the particulate filter while reducing release of excess nitrogen dioxide downstream of the particulate filter.

3. **The method of claim 1**, wherein the catalytic coating of the particulate filter comprises a selective catalytic reduction catalyst effective to reduce NOx with ammonia generated from decomposition or hydrolysis of urea.

4. **The method of claim 1**, wherein the diesel oxidation catalyst comprises at least one platinum-group metal supported on an oxide support, and wherein the oxidation activity is controlled by catalyst composition, catalyst volume, exhaust temperature, exhaust mass flow, or engine operating conditions.

5. **The method of claim 1**, wherein the additive comprises an aqueous urea solution injected into the exhaust gas upstream of the particulate filter and downstream of the diesel oxidation catalyst.

6. **The method of claim 1**, wherein the catalytic coating of the particulate filter comprises a soot oxidation catalyst and an SCR-active catalyst, such that particulate oxidation and NOx reduction occur within the particulate filter.

7. **The method of claim 1**, wherein the NO₂/NOx ratio downstream of the diesel oxidation catalyst is controlled to a value between about 0.2 and about 0.7.

8. **The method of claim 1**, further comprising monitoring at least one of exhaust temperature, NOx concentration, NO₂ concentration, oxygen concentration, particulate loading, or engine operating state, and adjusting additive dosing or engine operation in response thereto.

9. **The method of claim 1**, wherein carbon monoxide and unburned hydrocarbons are oxidized to carbon dioxide and water in the diesel oxidation catalyst before the exhaust gas reaches the particulate filter.

10. **The method of claim 1**, wherein nitrogen dioxide generated in the diesel oxidation catalyst reacts with carbon-containing particulate matter retained in the particulate filter to form carbon dioxide, carbon monoxide, or mixtures thereof.

A controller is configured to receive the detected NO2_1/NOx_1 value and actively adjust one or more combustion engine operating parameters, such as air-fuel ratio, exhaust gas recirculation rate, injection timing, injection quantity, boost pressure, or exhaust temperature, to drive the NO2_1/NOx_1 value toward a target range suitable for downstream selective catalytic reduction.
